one_line: Shared teacher-agent canvas for resource-aware tangible coding lessons.
what_it_does: Lets primary teachers and agents co-create, adapt, validate, and review screen-light coding missions under classroom constraints.
leverage_rationale: Structured tools share accepted lesson context, inventory, and staged proposals with the teacher; generic UI driving would be materially less precise and trustworthy.
leverage_evidence: Frame sheets show a shared Mission Builder canvas, setup/resource constraints, lesson summary, and structured-access diagrams.
About text describes pending proposals, teacher accept/edit/reject boundaries, and deterministic validation.
execution_rationale: The visible workflow is coherent from classroom setup through a populated, reviewable mission and printable-oriented outputs, though exact end-to-end tool results are not fully legible.
execution_evidence: Frames show progression through setup, structured lesson content, summary, and completed Lost Story Path mission.
About text specifies seven-step workflow and 13 validation checks.
impact_rationale: It addresses a concrete planning problem for primary teachers: aligning learning goals, class logistics, physical inventory, differentiation, and observable assessment.
impact_evidence: Frames visibly constrain a 24-pupil, 45-minute activity by limited robots, mats, and tile sets.
About text identifies teacher planning and review needs.
creativity_rationale: The human-in-the-loop, screen-light tangible-coding lesson canvas is a distinctive application of agent collaboration to physical classroom logistics.
creativity_evidence: Structured Access frames depict lesson context, tangible resources, mission content, and adaptations as first-class tools.
Lost Story Path workflow pursues the concept beyond generic lesson text generation.
usability_note: Clear card-based editor and persistent summary support review; some dense states may need refinement.
red_flags: Tool-call text is too small to independently verify exact payloads.
standouts: Inventory-aware lesson generation with explicit teacher approval boundary.
advance_reason: Strong educational fit, visible coherent workflow, and substantial WebMCP delta.

one_line: Source-backed personal decision agent across shopping, gifts, dates, travel, and staffing.
what_it_does: Collects deliberate personal context, searches authorized sources, preserves evidence, and returns recommendations while keeping consequential actions with the person.
leverage_rationale: Allowlisted origin tools and shared human-agent context make cross-source, evidence-preserving decisions more reliable than an agent scraping arbitrary pages.
leverage_evidence: About text describes origin allowlists, typed tools, personal context, and preserved source evidence.
Devpost screenshot shows a standalone workspace and shared human-agent UI.
execution_rationale: The broad product concept and packaging are coherent and appear implemented, with multiple decision workflows, though the supplied visual evidence is mostly presentation-level.
execution_evidence: Submission screenshot visibly presents Ribband branding and five use areas.
About text enumerates shopping, gifts, dates, vacations, and staffing workflows.
impact_rationale: Personal decisions routinely require combining preferences, constraints, and trustworthy facts; the intended audiences and use cases are specific and credible.
impact_evidence: About text gives concrete constraints such as budget, deadline, dislikes, prior activities, credentials, and schedule.
Product is framed around source-backed recommendations rather than generic search.
creativity_rationale: The synthesis of personal context, authorized web sources, and source-backed multi-domain decisions is a fresh interaction model.
creativity_evidence: One agent workspace spans shopping, gifts, dates, vacations, and project staffing.
Origin allowlisting and evidence preservation are central rather than cosmetic.
usability_note: Wide scope may create complexity, but the context-first model is understandable.
red_flags: Demo evidence is presentation-heavy and exact live outputs are not legible.
standouts: Source-backed decisions with explicit authorization boundaries.
advance_reason: High-value, distinctive agent/web interaction with credible breadth.

one_line: A browser DJ workstation that lets an agent compose, perform, listen, and verify a set.
what_it_does: Analyzes uploaded tracks, plans transitions, performs on two decks, reviews joins offline, and leaves humans full manual control.
leverage_rationale: The agent operates structured deck, mixer, analysis, review, and verification state; a generic UI agent could not comparably reliably perform this coordinated workflow.
leverage_evidence: Transcript explicitly says the agent called composition, review, and verification tools.
Frames show a two-deck DJ workstation and final loaded waveforms.
execution_rationale: The observable interface is substantial and coherent, with a detailed workflow and loaded two-deck states; audio quality itself is not assessable under the directive.
execution_evidence: 177-second transcript describes upload, compose, perform, review, repair, and verify.
Frames show decks, mixer, library, waveforms, and changing loaded states.
impact_rationale: It targets aspiring DJs and creators who want a usable starting set without mastering every technical control, while preserving human performance.
impact_evidence: Pitch and transcript identify the novice-friendly DJ goal.
Visible workstation exposes practical performance controls.
creativity_rationale: An agent that develops and audits a DJ set through a live booth is a memorable, ambitious interaction model beyond song generation.
creativity_evidence: About text describes mixability paths, drop-anchored clips, craft grammar, self-review, and repair.
Transcript frames agent and human as equivalent operators of the booth.
usability_note: Full DJ surface is coherent, though dense for beginners.
red_flags: Sonic quality and musicality are not assessable from silent contact sheets.
standouts: Closed-loop agent composition, verification, and human takeover.
advance_reason: Exceptional WebMCP leverage and creativity with strong observable product evidence.

one_line: An attestation ledger for recording which hand caused an action.
what_it_does: Classifies and records human, agent, script, unknown, and no-page provenance for WebMCP actions, with an approval desk and append-only relay ledger.
leverage_rationale: The product exists specifically to expose provenance that ordinary UI automation cannot reliably provide; shared structured attestation is the core capability.
leverage_evidence: Frames show Attestation desk, six registered tools, provenance categories, relay ledger, and pending approval.
About text explains the missing WebMCP identity/provenance signal and append-only records.
execution_rationale: The visible product has a coherent attestation workflow, ledger, tool registration, proposal, and approval states; backend validity is not independently proven by screenshots.
execution_evidence: Submission preview visibly shows categorized records and Awaiting approval panel.
About text describes 767 append-only records and correction semantics.
impact_rationale: Action provenance and trustworthy approval are real problems for deployment consoles and agentic systems, with value for operators and auditors.
impact_evidence: Frames show explicit unknown/script/agent attribution and approval UI.
About text grounds the problem in a human-approval bypass scenario.
creativity_rationale: The concept isolates a subtle but foundational identity gap in agent-mediated web actions and pursues it as a visible social-technical ledger.
creativity_evidence: Tagline and interface center the question of whose hand acted.
Append-only correction model preserves contradictory history rather than overwriting it.
usability_note: The provenance vocabulary is clear, though the underlying identity limits may confuse users.
red_flags: Screenshots cannot independently validate provenance against a real browser primitive.
standouts: Strongly framed provenance and approval problem with memorable ledger model.
advance_reason: Highly original and WebMCP-native infrastructure concept.

one_line: A cancellable trip finder that reports partial search results honestly.
what_it_does: Runs staged fare and stay searches across destinations, honors AbortSignal, returns partial reports on cancellation, and reserves booking for a human.
leverage_rationale: Abortable structured calls and first-class partial results give agents reliable control over long-running search that UI automation generally cannot provide.
leverage_evidence: About text specifies execute(args, signal), shared AbortController paths, and partial reports.
Pitch centers on cancellation semantics and agent awareness of unseen results.
execution_rationale: The described cancellation lifecycle is unusually specific and the visible product workflow is coherent, though exact frame details are limited.
execution_evidence: About text names catalogue, fare, stay, hold tools and human-only booking.
Facts confirm live demo and video frame sheets.
impact_rationale: Travel search is a real high-friction use case, and honest cancellation prevents wasted time and misleading completeness.
impact_evidence: Pitch gives concrete Bengaluru, budget, and duration query.
About text describes incremental cards and what was/was not searched.
creativity_rationale: Treating cancellation as a first-class, truthful result rather than an error is a strong and relevant interaction innovation.
creativity_evidence: Partial report and explicit unseen-search accounting are central design choices.
Human-only irreversible booking paired with reversible hold is thoughtful scope.
usability_note: Progressive results and multiple cancellation paths support control.
red_flags: Exact visual states were not independently legible at review time.
standouts: Correct cancellation semantics and honest partial-result contract.
advance_reason: Strong technical WebMCP use tied to a concrete travel workflow.

one_line: A WebMCP-enabled 3D/AR editor controlled by agents in the live authenticated session.
what_it_does: Lets agents create scenes, add assets, transform objects, adjust presentation, preview, and publish immersive web experiences alongside a human.
leverage_rationale: Structured editor commands operate live 3D state and publishable assets, a task where screenshot-driven UI automation is markedly unreliable.
leverage_evidence: About text lists typed scene, asset, transform, lighting, preview, and publish tools.
Pitch states the agent works inside the authenticated editor session while the user watches and undoes.
execution_rationale: The stated editor-to-publish workflow is coherent and the visual demo evidence shows a substantial product, though exact final publication proof is limited.
execution_evidence: About text gives an explicit user prompt → tool call → editor action → published experience flow.
Facts confirm live demo and multiple frame sheets.
impact_rationale: Small businesses and creators have a credible need for faster 3D/AR production without stitching specialist tools together.
impact_evidence: About text identifies creators and e-commerce teams as the audience.
Capabilities cover creation through publishing.
creativity_rationale: Bringing external agents into a live immersive editor is a strong, ambitious extension of agent-assisted creation.
creativity_evidence: Agent can manipulate scene graph, media, interactions, camera, and lighting through typed operations.
Human can observe, undo, and continue manual editing.
usability_note: Live shared editing and undo are helpful; 3D authoring remains inherently complex.
red_flags: Underlying editor predates the challenge; WebMCP addition is the new contribution.
standouts: Typed live-session control of a real 3D editor and publish pipeline.
advance_reason: High leverage and credible creator/e-commerce value.

one_line: An audio editor where agents inspect transcripts and propose surgical edits.
what_it_does: Detects silences and fillers, exposes transcript and timeline operations, proposes edits for approval, and exports audio/captions.
leverage_rationale: Structured word-level transcript and timeline tools let an agent make precise audio edits while sharing state with the editor; generic UI automation would be brittle.
leverage_evidence: About text specifies 43 WebMCP tools, word-level transcript editing, silence/filler detection, and approval.
Frames show audio-editor timeline and agent-oriented workflow states.
execution_rationale: The observable editor and described end-to-end edit/export loop are coherent; sonic quality is not assessable and does not affect this score.
execution_evidence: About text states the whole loop works end to end and supports local transcription.
Frame sheets show editor, transcript/timeline, and tool interaction surfaces.
impact_rationale: Creators and podcasters have a concrete recurring pain in removing ums, pauses, and bad takes; text-based editing can reduce that burden.
impact_evidence: About text identifies YouTube/audio creators and specific editing pain.
Product supports export of finished audio and captions.
creativity_rationale: Letting an agent hear semantically through transcript/timeline structure and propose reversible edits is a fresh interaction model for audio editing.
creativity_evidence: Agent edits audio by editing words and pauses rather than manipulating opaque waveform pixels.
Human approval remains central.
usability_note: Transcript-driven edits and approval can be approachable; editor complexity remains.
red_flags: Sonic quality, mixing, and timing feel are not assessable from silent evidence.
standouts: Semantic transcript-to-audio editing with local transcription option.
advance_reason: Strong practical workflow and meaningful structured-agent delta.

one_line: A local browser video studio where agents propose reviewable cuts and zooms.
what_it_does: Lets agents inspect footage and stage smart cuts, zooms, captions, overlays, voiceover, and music edits on a shared canvas before export.
leverage_rationale: Page-local tools can inspect browser-resident video and timeline state directly, avoiding fragile screenshot automation and large token transfer.
leverage_evidence: About text describes OPFS, Zustand, Canvas2D constraints and WebMCP toolcalls.
Frames show editor workspace, toolcall labels, timeline, zoom controls, and export UI.
execution_rationale: The studio presents a coherent editing surface with staged diffs and multiple production functions; precise end-to-end export proof is limited.
execution_evidence: Frames show workspace/editor, staged toolcall states, captions/overlays, and export menu.
About text specifies local decode, render, mixing, and export.
impact_rationale: Developers and product creators have a real need to turn raw recordings into concise demos with less manual scrubbing.
impact_evidence: About text quantifies the manual burden of demo editing.
Feature set directly targets cuts, zooms, captions, and framing.
creativity_rationale: Reviewable staged video diffs and browser-local agent inspection are a thoughtful, technically ambitious editing model.
creativity_evidence: Agent proposals are staged for human review rather than silently mutating the timeline.
100% local WebCodecs/Canvas2D architecture is part of the concept.
usability_note: Staged diffs and familiar timeline controls support safe iteration.
red_flags: Some frame text is small; export completion is not fully legible.
standouts: Local browser-native editing with reviewable agent diffs.
advance_reason: Strong fit between WebMCP and browser-resident media editing.

one_line: A storefront where agent purchases are governed by hash-chained receipts and human approval.
what_it_does: Supports agent catalog search, cart, policy-bound checkout, pending approval, abort, receipt polling, and post-order refund with a human-readable audit trail.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP supplies a typed, policy-bound, human-gated purchase channel sharing the same receipt state; ordinary browser automation cannot provide comparable governance.
leverage_evidence: About text explicitly describes request_checkout pausing mid-call, pending_approval, abort, standing rules, and get_recent_receipts.
Frame sheets show storefront/receipt and approval-oriented product states.
execution_rationale: The core commerce and governance workflow is unusually well specified and visibly packaged, though tamper-evidence/backend behavior is not independently testable here.
execution_evidence: About text specifies catalog, cart, checkout, approval, receipt polling, and refunds.
Facts confirm live demo and frame sheets; submission screenshot provides product packaging.
impact_rationale: Trust, accountability, and controllable delegation are central barriers to agentic commerce; shoppers have a specific real need for them.
impact_evidence: About text gives concrete standing rule example and live receipt trail.
Human can approve/deny purchases and undo via refund.
creativity_rationale: Combining commerce with a governed, hash-chained receipt trail and pausable tool calls is a distinctive and memorable interaction model.
creativity_evidence: Receipts make governance a first-class site capability rather than a generic audit log.
The same trail is readable by agent and human.
usability_note: Standing rules and one-tap approval can make delegation legible and safe.
red_flags: Cryptographic tamper-evidence is claimed in text but not independently verifiable from frames.
standouts: Human-gated, policy-bound commerce with shared receipts.
advance_reason: Top-tier leverage and impact on a concrete trust problem.

one_line: Typed WebMCP control of native Vulkan, ML, rendering, and motion applications.
what_it_does: Forwards bounded browser tool commands into a live native C++ OA runtime while keeping GPU state, tensors, and models local.
leverage_rationale: It bridges agents into native GPU application state that browser automation cannot meaningfully or reliably control; WebMCP is the essential boundary.
leverage_evidence: About text describes native C++ ownership of Vulkan device, graphs, models, rendering, and synchronization.
Typed adapter exposes bounded commands, metrics, identifiers, and verifiable results without moving large data.
execution_rationale: The architecture and two demonstration workspaces are coherent and technically intentional, with strong text evidence but limited legibility of final demo states.
execution_evidence: About text specifies model training/evaluation/checkpointing and prompt-to-motion workflows.
Facts confirm public repo, live demo, and video frame sheets.
impact_rationale: Researchers, developers, and creators using native GPU applications gain an important path to agent assistance without abandoning local compute or data control.
impact_evidence: About text names ML, media, and 3D applications as underserved by browser agents.
Bounded local execution addresses privacy and performance constraints.
creativity_rationale: Connecting WebMCP to live native Vulkan and ML/3D state is an ambitious architecture with a distinctive capability boundary.
creativity_evidence: The browser carries only bounded commands while native OA remains execution engine.
Combines training, rendering, video, and prompt-to-motion demonstrations.
usability_note: Typed bounded commands improve safety, but native ML/3D workflows are inherently specialized.
red_flags: OA runtime is pre-existing; review credits the WebMCP bridge rather than the whole runtime.
Exact tool calls are not legible in contact sheets.
standouts: Browser-to-native GPU bridge preserving live state and local data.
advance_reason: Exceptional leverage and technical ambition for agent-native native software.
